description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and the accuracy (ACC, %) (y-axis) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10³, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 60% to 85%, with tick marks at 60, 65, 70, 75, 80, and 85. The “Base” method (black line with circle markers) starts at approximately 64% at co-occurrence 0 and increases steadily to about 71% at 10³. The “FT” method (blue line with triangle-down markers) begins at ~65.5% and rises to ~73%. The “IKE” method (red line with triangle-up markers) starts at ~67.5% and reaches ~75.5%. The “MEND” method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at ~71% and climbs to ~80%. The “MEMIT” method (purple line with pentagon markers) starts at ~69.5% and increases to ~77.5%. The “ROME” method (green line with square markers) begins at ~74.5% and rises to ~83.5%, consistently outperforming all other methods across the entire range of co-occurrence numbers. All lines show a generally increasing trend, with steeper gains at lower co-occurrence numbers and diminishing returns as co-occurrence increases.
